div.div: One reserved core was saturated by three equal tenants, one of them our probe: moving the probe to a pool core freed the interaction service but cost the camera frames, so no placement is free on this layout
POOL: 8 shared cores [pool_cores, illustrative], shared by most services under CFS (the camera, the object detector, audio input ...); attribution to one pool core is approximate

RESERVED: 4 cores [reserved_cores, illustrative], removed from the general scheduler (isolcpus), services pinned by container cpuset. Board: an Orin-class board, 12 cores in all [board_cores, illustrative]

Full stack, pool as a whole
busy 0.8 of the pool [pool_busy_frac_full, illustrative]
run-queue wait 2 s per busy s [pool_wait_per_busy_full, illustrative] (camera-only row: 0.05 [pool_wait_per_busy_camera_only, illustrative])
-> a one-thread worker's CPU-second takes about 3 s of wall time (my estimate from `pool_wait_per_busy_full`: 1 + 2; summed wait is not latency for parallel threads)

reserved core A
middleware router (on every message path)
probe arm planned, not run

reserved core B, full stack: saturated
three groups, equal CFS shares = caps, not demands

reserved core C
the motor-control services (their own threads already queue)
never observers

reserved core D
the motor-control services' fast real-time bus loop
never observers
reserved cores A, C and D share the motor-control services' CPU cluster (shared cluster L3; page 04). Some late loops already on cores C-D.
probe move: reserved core B -> a pool core

Probe on reserved core B
(the service's core)

div.b: Interaction service, request accepted p50 [interaction_accepted_ms, illustrative]
Interaction service's main thread, run-queue wait
Probe receive delay p50 / p99 [probe_receive_delay_ms, illustrative]

div.div:
The interaction service's full-stack latency was an observer effect. About 90 % of the excess over alone came from the bench (my estimate from `interaction_accepted_ms`: (40 − 5) ÷ (40 − 2) ≈ 0.92). The service waited for its core behind our probe. The instrument (the request driver) did not wait, so the full-stack value was measured correctly; it was caused by us.
Pre-registered: core no longer saturated, met; p50 near alone, met; refutation rule not met.

No placement is free on this layout
reserved core B -> starves the interaction service (left column)
a pool core -> the camera loses frames (amber cells)
reserved cores C-D -> would compete with the motor loop at every wake-up (reasoning, not measured)
reserved core A -> middleware router + the motor cluster; not tested
Real fix: a lighter probe (not measured).

New full-stack baseline, both bench fixes (probe on a pool core + the dialogue engine's log filter, note A4): interaction service p50 5 ms [interaction_accepted_ms: probe_moved]; transcript p50 640 ms [transcript_latency_ms: full_filtered, illustrative]; the camera pays about 2 Hz for the observers on the pool.

Legend blue = pool core; grey = reserved core (thick dark border = motor-control services, never observers); amber dashed = our observers and what moving them costs; red-bordered column = probe on the service's core; green cells = what the move fixed.
Equal shares on a saturated core are what CFS gives groups that all want more: caps, not demands (the interaction service used more once its core had room). Every full-stack probe latency carries the probe's own receive delay, so it is an upper bound. Core letters A-D are labels, not core numbers.

Sources. Numbers loaded from ../constants.json by spec02.py; key in brackets. Note A1 (pool, reserved cores, equal shares); note A5 (probe placement, new baseline, the untested core). Two windows per arm. Background on the observer effect: ../../robot-workload-benchmarking/notes/B4 and C7.
Illustrative (round teaching numbers that keep the shape of a finding; not measurements): pool_cores, reserved_cores, board_cores, pool_busy_frac_full, pool_wait_per_busy_full, pool_wait_per_busy_camera_only, saturated_core_equal_share, interaction_accepted_ms, probe_receive_delay_ms, probe_cores_wanted, probe_on_pool_camera_cost_hz, transcript_latency_ms.
